And now the news in detail.
Prime Minister Narendra Modi today stated that India must innovate and lead the
world in shaping the technologies of tomorrow.
After inaugurating the emerging science, technology and innovation conclave in New Delhi,
Mr. Modi said that India must embrace the technologies of the future, innovate boldly
and lead the world in creating them.
He stressed that a vikasiddh Bharat will be built on strong foundations of scientific
research, discoveries and the spirit of innovation.
Mr. Modi said India aims to achieve self-reliance and build strength in critical technologies.
Prime Minister Modi visited different sections of the exhibition and interacted with the people
there.
The exhibition includes around 150 deep-tech start-ups stalls which highlight technological
developments and their potential applications across sectors.
The three-day conclave brings together leading scientists, researchers, academicians, policy
policymakers, industry leaders, startups and international experts to deliberate on emerging
technologies and India's science, technology and innovation priorities.
BRICS member nations have expressed deep concern over the continued escalation of tensions
in West Asia and called for exercising maximum restraint as well as avoiding actions
that could further aggravate the situation.
In the joint declaration which was unanimously adopted today at the 12th BRICS parliamentary
Forum held in New Delhi, the member countries urged to ensure the protection of civilians
and civilian infrastructure in accordance with the purposes and principles of the Charter
of the United Nations. The BRICS member countries said they encourage increasing efforts through
dialogue and diplomacy towards a long-term understanding that will contribute to lasting
peace, security and stability in the region.
A report.
BRICS nations have stressed on the need to work together to maintain smooth flow
global trade, supply chains and energy in accordance with applicable international law.
They have condemned the imposition of unilateral coercive measures that are contrary to international law.
The member nations highlighted the importance of the global south as a driver for positive change.
They reaffirmed the role of BRICS in voicing its concerns and priorities.
BRICS nations expressed strong condemnation of any acts of terrorism as criminal and unjustifiable.
They condemned the terrorist attack in Jammu and Kashmir on 22nd of April last year in
the strongest terms.
Bricks nations have urged to ensure zero tolerance for terrorism and reject double standards
in countering terrorism.
With Anand Kumar, Supena Sekhya, Akash Chani News, Delhi.
This is Aakash Vahani giving you the news.
Welcome back, you are listening to News at 9.

Dr. Mohapatra has cautioned people of destructive winds, heavy rainfall and coastal flooding.
The combined impact of heavy rainfall, wind and storms can lead to large-scale damage.
Therefore, it is advised to evacuate the people from the low-lying areas.
People should not move outside from today evening till the 28th moon.
During this time, cyclone will have the maximum intensity and maximum impact.
Meanwhile, IMT has issued a red-colour warning for extremely heavy rainfall over
coastal Andhra Pradesh, Orissa and Chhattisgarh tomorrow.
The Ministry of Home Affairs has directed state governments to keep a close watch, monitor
the situation in their areas regularly, and take appropriate precautionary measures in
view of the cyclone.
In an advisory, the ministry has suggested for evacuating the people living in coastal
areas to safer places and complete suspension of fishing operations.
In Andhra Pradesh, state authorities have stepped up preparedness as heavy to extremely

The cyclone was centered 170 km south-southeast of Vishakhapatnam this evening. Heavy too extremely

and Ankarpalli with isolated places likely to receive 21 cm or more of rainfall. The
state government is closely monitoring the situation, while district administrations
have established should control rooms and intensified preparedness and relief measures.
The State Disaster Management Authority has warned of seawater surges in vulnerable coastal
areas and urged fishermen and residents of low-lying areas to remain alert.
Meanwhile, more than 53 trains have been cancelled today and tomorrow as a precautionary measure.
R. Sai Girish for Aakashwari News, Vijay Vada.
In Odisha, the state government has mobilized disaster response teams and placed vulnerable

Rail services face widespread disruption, fishing operations have been suspended,

The administration is rushing against time to minimize damage and ensure public

India, remains a defining chapter in the country's history.

The Ministry of External Affairs said that they held extensive discussions today and
reviewed the entire spectrum of India and Liechtenstein relations.
The two leaders discussed ways to further deepen cooperation in key areas, including

They welcomed the positive momentum generated by the India-FTA TEPA and reaffirmed their
commitment to further strengthening the bilateral partnership.
India and Liechtenstein discussed proposals for double taxation avoidance agreement between

Bilateral engagement has steadily expanded to new areas of cooperation,

On to sports now. India's Aditya has won the gold at the World Under-19 Boxing Championships
in Montenegro. Aditya defeated Russia's Islam Magomedov by a 4-1 margin in the
men's 55kg final to claim the world title. Meanwhile, Meghashir Khan settled for silver
in the women's 80kg category. Earlier, Harshika won the bronze in the women's 65kg category,
while Prachi Tokas secured a bronze in the women's over 80kg category.
In men's cricket, India defeated Hearst New Zealand by six wickets in the 30-20 international
at Wellington today, taking an unassailable three-nil lead in the five-mast series.
Chasing a target of 199 runs, India stormed to victory in just 13.2 overs, losing four
wickets. Abhishek Sharma led the charge with a sensational 113 of just 38 balls, while his
opening partner, Veibhav Suryavanshi, smashed a cook fire 45 of 19 deliveries.
Earlier New Zealand posted 198 for the loss of three wickets in the stipulated 20 overs.
